land.text: the Zirid governorate of Ashir and the central Maghreb, from which Hammad ibn Buluggin broke away

predecessors.note: 'In 1014, Hammad declared his independence from Zirid suzerainty'; 'The Zirids failed to quash the rebellion and recognized Hammadid legitimacy in 1017.' The Zirid page dates the rebellion to 1015 and the peace to 1017.

land.text: the Hammadid country round Bejaia and Algiers

successors.note: 'The Almohads took Algiers in 1152 and captured Bejaia later the same year'; Yahya 'surrendered several months later, on 10 November 1152'.

capitals.name: Qal'at Bani Hammad
capitals.note: 'The fortress was built in 1007 by Hammad ibn Buluggin'; the Hammadid page: 'In 1007 and 1008, forces under Hammad left Ashir and built a new citadel-capital'. The state's span starts 1014 (independence). Abandoned in 1090 'under the menace of the Banu Hilal'.

capitals.name: Bejaia (Bougie)
capitals.note: 'Between 1067 and 1072 he built Bejaia' (al-Nasir); 'In 1090, with the Banu Hilal menace rising, the Hammadids moved their capital to Bejaia.'

correction.text: the 1018 outline taken back to 1014: Hammad's lands round Ashir and Qal'at Bani Hammad

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1014-1017: Cliopatria's first Hammadid shape begins in 1018, but 'In 1014, Hammad declared his independence' (infobox: 'Hammad proclaims independence from the Zirids: 1014'; the Zirid page: 1015) and the Zirids 'failed to quash the rebellion' before recognising it in 1017; the 1018 outline is taken back to 1014. Qal'at Bani Hammad 'sustained a siege from the Zirid in 1017'.

165,043 km2 for 1018-1055: the central Maghreb from Tiaret and the Chelif to Bejaia, Setif and Biskra with the Hodna; no infobox area exists to compare. In 1039 Hammama of Fez submitted to the Hammadids (outside the shape; recorded as a vassal in the ledger). Cliopatria's bbox reaches 17.7N, 9W, but that fragment holds no cell at gazetteer resolution in this shape.

164,949 km2 for 1056-1065, the same outline: the page's map caption reads 'Hammadid territories circa 1065, at their greatest extent during the reign of Al Nacir' (reigned 1062-1088). Valid 1056-1065.

correction.text: the 1056 outline plus Laribus (Le Kef), taken in 1066

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1066-1071 with the 1056 outline kept and Laribus added: Cliopatria drops the Hammadids to 32,833 km2 in 1066 and loses their capital Qal'at Bani Hammad (35.8N 4.5E), yet the page has them at their peak under al-Nasir and 'Sultan Al Nacer conquered the city of Laribus, near Kef, in 1066'; the capital stays at Qal'at Bani Hammad until 1090 (Qal'at page). The shrunken 1066 shape (Algiers, Bejaia, Chelif) is the coastal core only.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1090-1127: the coastal core round Algiers, Bejaia and the Chelif

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (32,683 km2, the coastal core: Algiers, Bejaia, the Chelif and the Setif edge) but valid 1090-1127 only: 'In 1090, with the Banu Hilal menace rising, the Hammadids moved their capital to Bejaia' and Qal'at Bani Hammad 'was abandoned under the menace of the Banu Hilal'. For 1072-1081 and 1082-1089 use the two new keyframes below, which keep the Hodna and Qal'at Bani Hammad. The Almohads partly destroyed the Qal'a only in 1152, so some Hammadid presence there is possible.
New keyframe 1072-1081: the 1056 outline and Laribus, the state at its peak with its capital at Qal'at Bani Hammad, before the Almoravids reach Tlemcen (1080/81) and Algiers (1082).

correction.text: the peak outline plus Laribus without the Oran-Tlemcen country

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1082-1089: the peak outline without the Oran-Tlemcen country, where the Almoravids stand from 1080-1083: 'by 1082 he had captured Algiers. Algiers became their easternmost outpost' (Almoravid page; the Yusuf page adds Tenes and Oran in 1082-83). Algiers itself stays in the shape and is hatched as an Almoravid occupation by the Almoravid dossier.
New keyframe 1128-1138: Tunis 'annexed in 1128 and controlled by Hammadid governors until 1148' joins the coastal core.

correction.text: the Algerian coastal core plus Tunis, without the stray Mauritanian cell

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1139-1146 as the coastal core plus Tunis, with a stray fragment removed: the shape's bbox reaches 17.6N, 8.9W and holds one cell in Mauritania (about 250 km2), an artefact in the Cliopatria row; the correction keeps only the Algerian part. 32,850 km2 against no infobox area.

correction.text: the Algerian coastal core plus Tunis, to 1148

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1147-1148: the same with Tunis, which 'Hammadid governors' held 'until 1148'. In 1144-1145 Hammadid troops had joined the Almoravids against the Almohads; the Almohads took Tlemcen and Oran in 1145 (Almoravid country, not Hammadid) and marched against the Hammadids in 1151.

New keyframe 1149-1152: the Algerian coastal core without Tunis, to the Almohad conquest: 'The Almohads took Algiers in 1152 and captured Bejaia later the same year'; Yahya surrendered on 10 November 1152. Cliopatria ends the row in 1151.

region.text: Hammad's lands round Ashir and Qal'at Bani Hammad

ledger.note: 1014: Hammad ibn Buluggin proclaims the Hammadid state. 'In 1014, Hammad declared his independence from Zirid suzerainty and switched his spiritual allegiance' to the Abbasids (the Zirid page: 'Hammad rebelled in 1015'). He had built the citadel Qal'at Bani Hammad in 1007-1008.

region.text: the Hammadid heartland round Ashir and the Hodna

ledger.note: 1015: the Zirid-Hammadid war. 'Hammad rebelled in 1015 and declared independence'; the Hammadid page names a 'Hammadid-Zirid War (1014-1018)' but describes no battles, and Qal'at Bani Hammad 'sustained a siege from the Zirid in 1017'.
1017: the Zirids make peace. 'The Zirids failed to quash the rebellion and recognized Hammadid legitimacy in 1017.'

region.text: the central Maghreb round Ashir and Qal'at Bani Hammad

ledger.note: 1017: the Zirids recognise Hammadid independence over the central Maghreb.
1039: Fez submits. 'In 1039, Hammama, ruler of Fez, submitted to the Hammadids after an attack by Qa'id ibn Hammad.'

1062: the submission of Fez is taken to end here. 'In 1062, Buluggin briefly took Fez before being assassinated by his cousin An-Nasir'; the page does not say what became of Hammama's Fez, so the end is the researcher's bridge (confidence 1).
1066: Laribus (Le Kef) conquered. 'Sultan Al Nacer conquered the city of Laribus, near Kef, in 1066.' The page does not name its previous holder; Cliopatria's Zirid 1056 shape covers Le Kef.

region.text: the Oran-Tlemcen country inside the Hammadid outline

ledger.note: 1082: the west of the peak outline passes to the Almoravids. 'By 1082 he had captured Algiers. Algiers became their easternmost outpost' (Almoravid page; the Yusuf page adds Tenes and Oran in 1082-83); the Hammadid page is silent. The region is the Oran-Tlemcen country inside the 1056 outline; Algiers itself stays Hammadid land under an Almoravid occupation.

1090: the capital moves from Qal'at Bani Hammad to Bejaia. 'In 1090, it was abandoned under the menace of the Banu Hilal'; the Hammadid page: 'In 1090, with the Banu Hilal menace rising, the Hammadids moved their capital to Bejaia.'

region.text: the Hodna, Zab and steppe country between the coastal core and the Sahara

ledger.note: 1090: the Hodna and the steppe round the old capital pass to the Arab nomads. 'In 1090, it was abandoned under the menace of the Banu Hilal'; the Banu Hilal page has the tribes spreading 'on the high plains of Constantine' and obstructing the Qal'a. The region is the part of the peak outline outside the coastal core; no page gives a boundary.

1103: the Hammadids contest Tlemcen. 'In 1103-1104 the Hammadids defeated the Almoravids and took control of Tlemcen.' The Almoravid page has a peace treaty with the Hammadids in 1104 and the Almohads taking Tlemcen from the Almoravids in 1144, so the control was brief or nominal.

1104: peace with the Almoravids. 'Eventually, in 1104, they signed a peace treaty with the Hammadids.' The Tlemcen page's timeline lists the Hammadid Emirate there 1015-1083 and the Almoravids from 1083.

1128: Tunis annexed. 'Tunis was annexed in 1128 and controlled by Hammadid governors until 1148.' The Zirid page has Tunis ruled by the Banu Khurasan dynasty, founded in 1059; the Hammadid page does not name the previous holder.

ledger.counterpart: Tunis (next holder not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1148: Tunis passes out of Hammadid hands. The page's 'until 1148' gives no successor; the Kingdom of Africa page has the Normans reaching 'the borders of Tunis' but not taking it.

region.text: the Hammadid country round Algiers and Bejaia

ledger.note: 1151: the Almohads march on the Hammadids. 'In 1151, he marched against the Hammadids' (Abd al-Mu'min).
1152: Algiers falls. 'The Almohads took Algiers in 1152 and captured Bejaia later the same year.'
1152: Bejaia, the capital, falls in August. 'In August 1152, he captured Bejaia, the capital of the Hammadids.' Qal'at Bani Hammad was 'partly destroyed by the Almohads in 1152' (Qal'at page).
1152: the fighting ends. Yahya 'surrendered several months later, on 10 November 1152 (10 Sha'ban 547 AH)'.

1152: the Hammadid dynasty ends. 'Conquered by the Almohads: 1152' (infobox); Yahya surrendered on 10 November. A brief revival in 1184 under 'Ali ibn Ghaniya was ended quickly (Hammadid page: 'quickly driven out'). Cliopatria's last year is 1151.

wars.name: Hammadid-Zirid War
wars.outcome: Hammadid success: the Zirids 'failed to quash the rebellion and recognized Hammadid legitimacy in 1017'; the Zirid page: a 1017 peace let Hammad keep effective independence.
wars.note: The page gives no battles; the Qal'a page has a Zirid siege of the fortress in 1017.

wars.name: Hammadid control of Fez
wars.outcome: Hammama of Fez submitted in 1039; Buluggin 'briefly took Fez' in 1062 and was assassinated by An-Nasir. No lasting territorial result.

wars.name: Hammadid conquest of Laribus
wars.outcome: Al-Nasir took Laribus near Kef in 1066.
wars.note: The previous holder is not named; the Zirid and Hammadid pages say nothing more.

wars.name: Hilalian pressure on the Hammadid steppe
wars.outcome: The Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym defeat the Zirids at Haydaran on 14 April 1052 (Zirid page); the Banu Hilal page has them spreading 'on the high plains of Constantine' and obstructing Qal'at Bani Hammad, which is abandoned in 1090 (Qal'a page).
wars.note: The Hammadid page does not mention the Hilalian invasion and the Banu Hilal page gives no years; the span is the Zirid page's 1052 battle to the Qal'a page's 1090.

wars.name: Hammadid-Almoravid war over Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Hammadid success at Tlemcen in 1103-1104 per the Hammadid page; peace treaty in 1104 per the Almoravid page.

wars.name: Genoese and Norman raids on the Hammadid coast
wars.outcome: 'The Genoese also raided Bejaia (1136)'; 'the Kingdom of Sicily occupied Djidjelli' (undated on the page); the Bejaia page says the Hammadid fleet 'slowed down European advances'. No lasting loss.
wars.note: The span is the one dated raid (the Genoese in 1136); the page gives no year for the Sicilian occupation of Djidjelli.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of the Hammadids
wars.outcome: Hammadid forces join the Almoravids against the Almohads in 1144-1145 without success; Abd al-Mu'min marches on the Hammadids in 1151, takes Algiers and Bejaia in 1152 and receives Yahya's surrender on 10 November 1152.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened: the steppe edge is nomad country, the western edge moves with the Almoravids (Tlemcen, Algiers) and the eastern edge with the Zirids and Hilalians; the coast is the only fixed side.

sources.title: Hammadid dynasty
sources.note: Identity, infobox dates (1014, 1152), capitals, the Zirid war, Fez 1039, Laribus 1066, Bejaia 1067-72, Tlemcen 1103-04, Tunis 1128-1148, the Almohad conquest and 10 November 1152.

sources.title: Qal'at Bani Hammad
sources.note: The capital built in 1007, the Zirid siege of 1017, abandonment in 1090, partial destruction in 1152; no territory on the page.

sources.title: Banu Hilal
sources.note: Thin: no years for Haydaran or the Hammadids; spreading on the Constantine plains and obstructing the Qal'a.

sources.title: Bejaia
sources.note: Bejaia founded 1067 by al-Nasir, Almohad seizure 1152, Banu Ghaniya seizure 1183.

sources.title: Zirid dynasty
sources.note: Hammad's rebellion in 1015 and the 1017 peace; Banu Khurasan at Tunis from 1059; Haydaran 14 April 1052.

sources.title: Almoravid dynasty
sources.note: Peace treaty with the Hammadids in 1104; Algiers taken by 1082.

sources.title: Almohad Caliphate
sources.note: Bejaia captured in August 1152, the Battle of Setif in April 1153.

sources.title: Tlemcen
sources.note: Timeline: Hammadid Emirate 1015-1083, Almoravids 1083-1147; conflicts with the Hammadid page's 1103-04.

notes: Cliopatria's Hammadid row shrinks from 165,000 to 32,800 km2 in 1066 and loses the capital Qal'at Bani Hammad, while the page dates the peak to about 1065 and the move of the capital to 1090; keyframes 1066, 1072b and 1082 restore the larger outline from the 1056 shape until 1090, and the 1072 coastal shape is kept for 1090-1127. The Hammadid shape from 1066 contains Algiers; two Almoravid pages say the Almoravids took Algiers by 1082 (recorded by the Almoravid dossier as an occupation to 1104). No mirrored Hammadid event is entered because the Hammadid page is silent on it. The Tlemcen page's timeline lists the Hammadid Emirate there 1015-1083, which contradicts the Hammadid page ('In 1103-1104 the Hammadids ... took control of Tlemcen') and the Almoravid pages (Almoravid Tlemcen from 1080/81 to 1144); no Hammadid keyframe includes Tlemcen except as a contested zone 1103-04. Dates differ: independence 1014 (Hammadid infobox) vs 1015 (Zirid page and Hammadid rulers table); founding of Qal'at Bani Hammad 1007 (Qal'a page) vs 1007-1008 (Hammadid page); end 1152 (infobox) vs Cliopatria 1151. Not covered by the pages opened: the Hilalian invasion's effect year by year (the Hammadid page does not mention it), the capture of Constantine by al-Nasir (undated), Biskra, Ouargla and the Zab, the Norman occupation of Djidjelli (undated), Tunis after 1148. The 1184 revival under 'Ali ibn Ghaniya belongs to the Almoravid dossier (Banu Ghaniya). Counterparts without a dossier: Banu Khurasan of Tunis (1059-1128), Hammama of Fez. Rulers not entered: the Hammadid page's ruler table was not read in full (it gives al-Nasir 1062-1088 and Yahya at the end, with 1007 and 1015 as the start). Method note: every page was read through WebFetch, which returns a model-made extraction; phrases in quotation marks are the extraction's wording of the page and may differ in small ways from the live text, while the years and months are the ones it reported.
